newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia yet to sign gem export decree - Finance Min.
newsitem.headline: Russia yet to sign gem export decree - Finance Min.

text.p: Russia has yet to sign a decree outlining diamond exports from the beginning of June until the end of the year, Vladimir Rybkin, head of the precious metals and stones section at the Finance Ministry, said on Friday.

On a visit earlier this month to the autonomous diamond-producing region of Yakutia, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais, who is also Finance Minister, said the export quota decree would be signed by the end of May.
"The decree has not yet been signed," Rybkin said.
He said the decree was unlikely to be signed on Friday, and that he could not be sure that it would be signed by the end of Saturday, the last day in May.
"But I do expect the decree to be signed soon. There are only technical questions still to resolve," he said.
Earlier this month Russia's dominant diamond producer Almazy Rossii-Sakha (ARS) said the government had signed a decree freeing up exports of gems up until the end of May.
South African diamond giant De Beers bought gems from ARS during the first four months of the year, but was unable to export them until May because of the absence of an export decree.
ARS and De Beers are also awaiting final government approval for a long-delayed gem trade deal, held up since the beginning of the year.
De Beers sharply curtailed purchases of diamonds from ARS at the end of last year after Moscow failed to communicate its position on a draft agreement submitted to the government in October 1996.
Chubais said the deal would be signed by June 4.
